answer: In an agent marketplace, agents such as mesa, haven, and juniper vote on payments in proportion to escrowed collateral, not account count. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities therefore buys no extra voting power. Deposits stay locked through a dispute window, and signed votes approving conflicting payments trigger slashing. To gain majority control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more collateral than honest voters, risking its loss if they double-sign.
